findings: [Architecture / Feature Boundary & Default Compatibility] In source/crates/mori/Cargo.toml, gating mori-backend, mori-ledger, futures, rand, and the 8 Midnight SDK crates under `native` with `default = ["native"]` preserves 100% of default and explicit-native CLI behavior while allowing `-p mori --no-default-features` to compile without Midnight crates in its selected package graph. Because Cargo does not support optional dev-dependencies, promoting the 8 SDK dev-dependencies (`midnight-ledger`, `midnight-base-crypto`, `midnight-coin-structure`, `midnight-onchain-state`, `midnight-onchain-runtime`, `midnight-storage`, `midnight-transient-crypto`, `midnight-serialize`) to optional normal dependencies enabled by `native` is necessary so SDK-free test compilation (`cargo test --frozen -p mori --no-default-features --test ...`) does not pull the Midnight closure. `k256` in `source/crates/mori-core/Cargo.toml` must remain unconditional because legacy `intent`/`verify-intent` and Core tests rely on `k256::{ecdsa, schnorr}`.

[Error & Process Exit Contract Verification] Verified against `source/crates/mori/src/error.rs` and `source/crates/mori/src/main.rs`: `CliError::Operation { code: String, message: String }` uses struct fields directly (`#[error("{code}: {message}")]`) and has no `with_code` method. `main()` renders any `Err(report)` from `commands::run` via `shell.report(&report)` to stderr and returns `ExitCode::FAILURE` (OS exit 1), never emitting a JSON error on stdout and never returning exit code 2 (which is reserved for Clap parse/validation failures prior to `commands::run`). The proposed unavailable helper returning `CliError::Operation { code: "mori::command::native-unavailable".into(), message: "This mori build has no Midnight support. Rebuild with the native feature enabled.".into() }.into()` matches the exact source error pipeline with empty stdout, stderr diagnostic, exit 1, zero file I/O, and no semantic fallback.

[Explicit Policy Assessment: No-Native `inspect --target` Pre-Read Refusal vs. Post-Read Profile Alternative] In `source/crates/mori/src/commands/inspect.rs`, `run` currently calls `read_source(&args.file)` first, handles source-only `moriarty/2`, and then (when `args.target.is_some()` on a `moriarty/2` source) returns the Core profile error (`mori::core::profile`) before reading `--target`. The design's policy decision—returning `mori::command::native-unavailable` in no-native builds as soon as `args.target.is_some()` BEFORE `read_source(&args.file)` (even for `moriarty/2` inputs), while keeping native/default ordering and source-only `inspect` untouched—is superior to the post-read profile alternative for two reasons: (1) Security/gating side-effect discipline: it enforces a uniform zero-I/O boundary across all disabled native routes in `--no-default-features` builds, preventing `inspect --target` from acting as a 1 MiB filesystem read/existence oracle on a disabled capability; (2) Clean compilation boundary: gating the entire post-read `--target` branch, `core1_refusal()`, and all enforcement-map helpers (`encoded`, `reference`, `enforcement_report`, `action_report`, `public_field`, `authorization_rule`, `statement_rule`, `expression_constraints`, `unknown_premises`) under `#[cfg(feature = "native")]` eliminates dead-code paths in no-native builds while preserving `h16_core_two_inspect_target_refuses_with_core_profile_before_target_read` in native/default builds.

[Mixed-Command Pure Argument Precedence & Concrete Code Check in `intent.rs`] Verified pure argument validation precedence before capability refusal in mixed commands (`simulate.rs`, `intent.rs`, `verify_intent.rs`): (1) In `simulate.rs`, Clap handles `--resume`/`--event` requirements and conflicts and `--logical-cap` parsing/conflicts (exit 2, no I/O); in `simulate::run`, `--trace` without `--target` must continue to fail with `--trace requires --target` before the no-native `run_trace` stub returns `mori::command::native-unavailable`, and `--target` or signed authorization flags without `--trace` retain `--target and signed replay arguments require --trace` before source read. (2) In `verify_intent.rs`, `run()` checks `(Some(_), None)` (`--profile moriarty-jubjub-owner-intent/1 requires --target`) and `(None, Some(_))` before calling `signed(&args, target)`, so a no-native `signed` stub automatically preserves pure argument checks first. (3) In `intent.rs`, however, the check `let (Some(target), Some(at)) = (&args.target, args.at) else { return Err(super::core_io::operation("--profile moriarty-jubjub-owner-intent/1 requires --target and --at together")); };` currently sits inside `fn signed(args: Args, _shell: &mut Shell)` (lines 153-157). During implementation, that `--target` and `--at` presence check must either be hoisted into `intent::run` before dispatching to `signed` or retained at the top of the no-native `signed` function before returning `mori::command::native-unavailable`, so missing `--target`/`--at` under `--profile` continues to report the argument error before build unavailability.

[Helper & Test Module `cfg` Hygiene Under `-D warnings`] Verified exact helper and test dependencies across `source/crates/mori/src/commands/` and `source/crates/mori/tests/`: (1) In `core_io.rs`, `review_identity` must stay unconditional (used by legacy `intent.rs`), whereas `key_export_identity` is only called by `ledger_operation` and must be gated under `#[cfg(feature = "native")]` alongside `ledger_operation`, `signed_target`, `authority`, `signed_intent`, `key_export_diagnostic_tests`, and `degree_diagnostic_tests`. (2) In `signed_call_io.rs`, `mod tests` (`nonce_v2_cli_frame_option_is_explicit_and_v2_only`) imports `SignedVersion` from `mori_ledger::signed::*` and calls `Input::validate_frame_mode`, so both `validate_frame_mode` and `mod tests` require `#[cfg(feature = "native")]`. (3) In `tests/core_continuations.rs`, `const SIGNED_TARGET` (line 496) is used only by `h18_core_two_compile_signed_target_is_unsupported_before_output_directory` and must be gated with `#[cfg(feature = "native")]` to avoid unused-constant warnings under `--no-default-features`; `fn diagnostic` (line 366) will remain used if called by the new `#[cfg(not(feature = "native"))]` `inspect --target` availability test. (4) In `tests/fee_pool_component.rs`, `fn status_text` (line 72) is called only by `public_source_static_all_actions_and_separate_process_reopen_both_programs` and must be gated under `#[cfg(feature = "native")]` together with `static_command` and the two `compile-call` tests. (5) For the 11 native-only test targets (`check_compile_io`, `check_static_compile_io`, `prepare_call`, `installed_call`, `signed_installed_call`, `native_proofs`, `signed_intents`, `replay`, `replay_challenge`, `enforcement_report`, `mapped_role_static_io`), declaring `[[test]]` with `required-features = ["native"]` in `crates/mori/Cargo.toml` is the cleanest single convention so Cargo omits those targets from `--no-default-features` test selection automatically.

[Guideline Exceptions, Fixture Provenance & Capture Hooks] Confirmed against `source/RUST_GUIDELINES.md`: (1) Line 252 (`Never write tests that invoke the CLI binary, and never snapshot --help`) conflicts with existing `CARGO_BIN_EXE_mori` integration tests and Issue #81's requirement for real CLI binary checks; recording the narrow exception for public command boundary tests (frozen output/exit/I/O and feature availability, while keeping `--help` snapshot prohibition and library unit-test rules intact) is necessary and appropriately scoped. (2) Line 228 (`Nothing under crates/ reads files outside it; copy anything needed in`) conflicts with `tests/stage_test_public.rs` (`../../models/core-stage-tests`), `tests/core_continuations.rs` (`../../../examples/core/continuations/...`), `tests/fee_pool_component.rs`, and `tests/core_test_report.rs` (`../../examples/core/fee-pool`); this provenance gap is accurately flagged for explicit disposition. (3) Existing tests contain opt-in environment capture hooks (`MORI_FEE_POOL_CAPTURE_DIR` in `fee_pool_component.rs`, `MORI_METERED_INTENT_EVIDENCE` in `metered_intents.rs`, `MORI_INIT_CAPTURE_DIR` in `init.rs`) that perform filesystem writes when those variables are set; future test runs must ensure clean environment state.
